summary: Lunar Landing Site Navigator helps mission planners choose where to land at the Moon's south pole, where the Sun skims the horizon and crater walls can cut a lander's power and its link to Earth. For four Artemis III candidate sites we traced each site's real 360° horizon from NASA LRO LOLA terrain data and computed hour-by-hour Sun and Earth positions from JPL Horizons. The web app shows a 3D Moon, a first-person view of each site's horizon, a 60-day sunlight and Earth-link calendar, a battery simulation, and a "story mode" that tests whether a lander survives. We checked our results against NASA's LOLA illumination maps. A tabletop model (Arduino turntable, servo-driven Sun and a crater wall printed from real terrain) is driven live from the app, and its light sensor confirms each prediction physically.
details:
• How it works: LOLA polar elevation model (240 m) → ray-cast horizons out to 320 km with the Moon's curvature → JPL Horizons hourly Sun and Earth positions → % sunlit, longest darkness, Earth-link windows and best 14-day landing window → compared with the NASA illumination map.
  • Tools: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Three.js, Node.js data scripts, Web Serial API, Arduino (C++), 28BYJ-48 stepper, SG90 servo, LDR sensor.
  • Creative part: the physical model is a real-data check. The printed crater wall is the site's true horizon, and the app compares the sensor's reading with its own prediction live.
  • Impact: quickly shows which sites keep power and comms through a mission, and why.
  • Factors considered: the 60-day window vs long-term averages, 240 m terrain resolution, a 2 m observer height, and an accessible colourblind-safe calendar.
